text_blocks.snippet: ST-segment depression of 0.6 mm in three contiguous leads on an electrocardiogram (ECG) is generally considered suggestive of myocardial ischemia. While a depression of 0.5 mm or more in two contiguous leads is often used as a threshold for ischemia, 0.6 mm in three leads increases the likelihood of a significant cardiac event. Further investigation and clinical correlation are necessary to determine the specific cause and appropriate management.
